_comment: Shared Naive padding-protocol test vectors.
This file is the machine-checkable contract between the two independent
implementations of the Naive padding protocol:
A. klzgrad/forwardproxy  (the reference)  - branch naive, commit
B. sing-box Native Naive inbound          - protocol/naive/inbound_conn.go
C. cronet-go Naive outbound               - naive_conn.go (this repository)
B and C agreeing with each other is NOT sufficient evidence of correctness: two
implementations can share the same mistake and interoperate perfectly while both
diverging from the wire format the reference produces. Every expectation below is
therefore derived from A, whose AddPadding branch is:
paddingSize := rand.Intn(256)
maxRead     := 65536 - 3 - paddingSize
nr, er      := src.Read(buf[3:maxRead])
if nr != nw { err = io.ErrShortWrite }
Consumers must read the expectations from this file rather than restating them,
so that a change to the protocol shows up as a diff here.
Both implementations' tests load this file. It is duplicated verbatim into
sing-box at test/jiejie/reference/naive_padding_vectors.json; the copies are
byte-identical and a test in each repository compares them by content hash.

invariants.statement: frame_header_size + payload + padding <= max_frame_size for every frame
a frame's payload never exceeds the budget implied by its own padding draw
front headroom, MTU and rear headroom describe exactly one maximal frame
the full 0..255 padding range is reachable and is not clamped to fit a buffer
a Write returning n < len(p) with a nil error is a failure
the padding frame counter advances only for frames wholly written
exactly padding_count frames are framed; the remainder is raw

chunking_cases.note: one byte over the padding-255 budget spills into a second frame
one byte over the padding-127 budget spills into a second frame
one byte over the padding-0 budget spills into a second frame
two full frames plus a remainder
